title: [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois..., pages 650 bis à 787, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (continuation of the 'Longue Marche' manuscript). We have a germ of a differentiable surface (X,x). Attached to it are:
- S_x, a topological circle, apparently the circle of directions (half-lines) at x;
- D*_x, the germ of punctured neighbourhood of x;
- T_x, a free Z-module of rank 1, the common fundamental group or deck group, i.e. the 'local monodromy' lattice.
The notations S_x^~ and D*_x^~ denote universal coverings, which are T_x-torsors over S_x and over D*_x. 𝒜_x is a family of arcs A of the circle S_x. Ep(A) is the sector germ (épointé) in D*_x lying over A. A 'corrélation' h_x between a covering of S_x and a covering of D*_x is a compatible bijection between sections over each arc A and sections over the sector Ep(A). Diagram (117), on an earlier page, says that triples (covering of S_x, covering of D*_x, correlation) form a category equivalent, via either projection, to coverings of S_x and to coverings of D*_x. This is a canonical, sector-wise form of the homotopy equivalence between the link circle and the punctured germ.

On this page: let u:(X,x)→(X',x') be an isomorphism of germs. It induces u_S on the direction circles, u_{D*} on the punctured germs and u_T on the lattices. Define:
- F(u), the set of lifts of u_S to the universal covers;
- G(u), the set of lifts of u_{D*} to the universal covers.
Both are T_x-torsors. The aim is a canonical iso of T_x-torsors F(u) ≅ G(u) (120): lifting the map on directions is the same as lifting the map on the punctured germ.

Proof:
1. By transport of structure, the pullbacks S_x'^~ = u_S^*S_{x'}^~ and D_x^{*'~} = u_{D*}^*D_{x'}^{*~} carry a correlation h'_x.
2. Hence F(u) ≅ Isom_{S_x}(S_x^~, S_x'^~) and G(u) ≅ Isom_{D*_x}(D_x^{*~}, D_x^{*'~}) (121).
3. By the equivalence (117), the Isom set between the triples (S^~, D*^~, h) and (S'^~, D*'^~, h') maps bijectively, T_x-equivariantly, onto both (122). This gives (120). Grothendieck notes it yields an earlier construction (96).

Characterisation (123): take lifts u_{S~} and u_{D*~} associated under (120). Take an arc A with image A', a section α of S_x^~ over A, and β the section over Ep(A) corresponding to α under h_x. Transport α and β to α' and β'. Then α' and β' correspond under h'.

The next page uses this to define the identification directly for a fixed A and α, and checks independence of α (by T-equivariance) and of A. Independence of A follows because inclusion generates the coarse equivalence relation on arcs.

Purpose: a canonical, functorial identification of the local fundamental group or torsor of the punctured germ with that of the circle of directions. This is a differentiable precursor of 'tangential base points' needed for the Teichmüller-tower / Galois action constructions.
errors: No mathematical errors. The torsor structures on F(u) and G(u) are really under T_x' or T_x via u_T. Grothendieck tacitly uses u_T to treat everything as T_x-torsors, which is harmless.
The '(170)' on the next page is presumably a misreading or mis-writing of (120).

ideas.what: Canonical equivalence between coverings of the circle of directions and coverings of the punctured germ, realised by a sector-wise 'correlation' of sections over arcs A and sectors Ep(A)
ideas.modern_name: Link/punctured-neighbourhood homotopy equivalence; real blow-up (oriented blow-up) at a point; tangential base points
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical topology. Tangential base points: Deligne (1989); also Ihara and Nakamura in the anabelian context
ideas.where_published: La Longue Marche (1981) manuscript itself. Esquisse d'un programme alludes to base points 'at infinity' or tangential.

ideas.what: Canonical isomorphism of torsors of lifts F(u) ≅ G(u) for an isomorphism of surface germs, with an explicit sector-wise characterisation
ideas.modern_name: Functoriality of tangential base points under diffeomorphisms of germs

deep.surprise_reason: A careful, routine torsor and transport-of-structure verification of the canonical identification between direction-circle coverings and punctured-germ coverings. It is foundational bookkeeping for tangential base points and contains nothing new to specialists.
transcription_corrections: Page number '783' is at the top. The archive folio is 270.
'Les pr. 2[?]' is uncertain. It may read 'Leur proj.' or similar, introducing the canonical isomorphisms (121).
(122) should read 'G(u_x) = Isom(D_x^{*~}, D_x^{*'~})' with closing parentheses. The handwriting is consistent with this.
